thread_title: S. flava rugelii MK F17 Milton, FL (copper  tinge)
breadcrumb: S. flava rugelii MK F17 Milton, FL (copper  tinge)

posts.body_html:
Here's a clone, originally from Mike King's collection, of S. flava var. rugelii that has an unusual copper tinge to the lid and parts of the "body" of the trap. There's a lot of S. x moorei hybrids in the wild in that area, so I suspect it is likely that there are moorei genes that were historically mixed into this plant.

posts.body_html:
That's a new one to me! Very interesting. Does the colour on the hood fade as the season advances being strong only at the start of the pitcher's cycle?

The tubes are a nice fluted form too. Great looking clone.

posts.body_html:
I don't know-this is the first year that this plant has produced some significant pitchers. I think I got it in 2011, and I don't remember it having the bronze color until now. Perhaps the pitchers were too small before.

Maybe our European friends who have had more experience with this plant can chime in?
